title: Equivalent fractions: same amount, different names

pedagogy.rationale: Folding paper strips (concrete) and comparing strip pictures (pictorial) come before the multiply-top-and-bottom rule (abstract).

prerequisiteAssumptions: Learners can name a fraction as equal parts of one whole (concept g4-fractions-equal-parts).

misconceptions.description: Adds the same number to the top and bottom, thinking 1/2 = 2/3.
misconceptions.response: Fold or draw both fractions: 2/3 covers more of the strip than 1/2. Multiplying both parts keeps the amount the same; adding does not.

misconceptions.description: Thinks 4/8 is more than 1/2 because the numbers are bigger.
misconceptions.response: Line the strips up: 4/8 and 1/2 reach exactly the same point.

scenes.title: Who got more cassava bread?
scenes.learnerAction: Predict who got more before reading on.

content.body:
Fatu cut her cassava bread into 2 equal pieces and ate 1. Boima cut the same size bread into 4 equal pieces and ate 2.

Boima says he ate more because 2 is more than 1. Is he right? Make a guess before you go on.

accessibility.textAlternative: Fatu ate 1 of 2 equal pieces; Boima ate 2 of 4 equal pieces of the same bread. Who ate more?

scenes.title: What you will be able to do

content.body: By the end of this lesson you will be able to:
keyPoints: Show that two fractions name the same amount using strips or drawings.
Write equivalent fractions by multiplying the top and bottom by the same number.

accessibility.textAlternative: Goal: show and write equivalent fractions, using strips first and then multiplication.

scenes.title: Fold a strip
scenes.learnerAction: Fold a paper strip and shade it as you open each step.

content.body: Take a paper strip. Follow each step with your own strip, then open the next step.

steps.label: Fold in half
steps.description: Fold the strip once and shade one part: you have shaded 1/2.

steps.label: Fold again
steps.description: Fold it in half again without unfolding. Open it: there are 4 equal parts and 2 are shaded. 2/4 covers the same part as 1/2.

steps.label: Fold a third time
steps.description: Fold again: 8 equal parts, 4 shaded. 4/8 is still the same shaded part.

hints: Keep the shading the same; only the folds change.
scenes.expectedObservation: Learners see the same shaded length named 1/2, 2/4 and 4/8.

accessibility.textAlternative: Folding a strip in half, then again and again, the same shaded part is 1/2, then 2/4, then 4/8.
accessibility.keyboardPath: Each step is a button; press Enter to open it in order.

offline.note: Paper strips are the core modality; the fraction visualizer is optional.

scenes.title: Line the strips up
scenes.learnerAction: Open each row of the strip picture and compare where the shading ends.

content.body: Picture three strips of the same length, one under the other. Open each row and look at where the shading stops.

steps.label: Row 1: 1/2
steps.description: One of two equal parts is shaded; the shading stops at the middle.

steps.label: Row 2: 2/4
steps.description: Two of four equal parts are shaded; the shading also stops at the middle.

steps.label: Row 3: 4/8
steps.description: Four of eight equal parts are shaded; again the shading stops at the middle. All three name the same amount: they are equivalent fractions.

accessibility.textAlternative: Three equal strips: 1/2, 2/4 and 4/8 shaded. In each, the shading ends at the middle, so the fractions are equivalent.
accessibility.keyboardPath: Each row is a button; press Enter to open it.

offline.note: Described in text; learners can draw the strips.

scenes.title: The multiplying rule
scenes.learnerAction: Read the rule and the example.

content.body:
Each fold doubled the number of parts and doubled the shaded parts. That is the rule: **multiply the top and the bottom by the same number** and the amount stays the same.

1/2 = (1 × 3)/(2 × 3) = 3/6.

Adding the same number does not work: 1/2 is not 2/3.
keyPoints: Multiply top and bottom by the same number.
Never add the same number to top and bottom.

accessibility.textAlternative: Multiply the numerator and the denominator by the same number to get an equivalent fraction: 1/2 times 3 over 3 is 3/6. Adding does not work.

scenes.title: Quick check
scenes.learnerAction: Choose an answer for each question.

content.body: Choose an answer. Read the feedback, even when you are right.

options.feedback: 2/4 is the same as 1/2, which is more than 1/3.
That doubles only the top. Multiply the top and the bottom.
1/6 is smaller: the bottom changed but the top did not.

items.prompt: Back to the bread: did Boima (2/4) eat more than Fatu (1/2)?

options.feedback: Bigger numbers do not mean a bigger amount. Line up the strips.

options.text: No, they ate the same amount
options.feedback: Yes. 2/4 and 1/2 are equivalent: the same amount of bread.
Look at the strips again: the shading stops at the same place.

accessibility.textAlternative: Two questions: which fraction equals 1/3, and whether 2/4 is more than 1/2.
accessibility.keyboardPath: Tab to each option and press Space; feedback is read aloud.

scenes.title: Make your own equivalent fractions
scenes.learnerAction: Write two equivalent fractions for each fraction.

content.body: Write two fractions equivalent to each fraction. Show the multiplication you used.

hints: Try multiplying the top and bottom by 2, then by 3.

accessibility.textAlternative: Write two equivalent fractions for 2/5 and for 3/4 in the text boxes, showing the multiplication.
accessibility.keyboardPath: Tab to each text box and type.

offline.note: Answers are kept on this device.

scenes.title: Explain it in your own words

content.body: Write a short answer. There is no single right wording.

prompts.prompt: Explain to Boima why 2/4 and 1/2 are the same amount.

accessibility.textAlternative: Write an explanation of why 2/4 and 1/2 are the same amount.
accessibility.keyboardPath: Tab to the text box and type.

content.body: Answer the question. Your answer is checked by the school's learning system, not on this device.

accessibility.textAlternative: A final multiple-choice question on equivalent fractions, answered with keyboard or touch.
accessibility.keyboardPath: Tab to each option and press Space.

offline.note: An answer given on a device is scored after reconnecting; without a device the teacher gives the same question on paper.

fallback.content: Your teacher gives the same question on paper and records your answer.
